topic: The Infinite in a Finite Box: An Introduction to Space-Filling Curves
target_audience: Undergraduate students in mathematics or computer science

outline.topic: The Infinite in a Finite Box: An Introduction to Space-Filling Curves
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate students in mathematics or computer science

sections.title: The Dimensional Paradox (Prerequisites)
sections.content: Establish the standard intuition: a 1D line has length but no area, and a 2D square has area. Pose the question: Can a continuous, non-overlapping line visit every single point in a square area?
sections.example: An ant walking on a 1x1 grid, trying to touch every coordinate without lifting its legs.

sections.title: The Peano Construction (Iterative Logic)
sections.content: Introduce the concept of 'Iterative Fractals'. Explain that we start with a simple generator and apply it infinitely. Show how at each step (n=1, 2, 3), the line gets increasingly 'wiggly', filling more of the square.
sections.example: Visual animation: A single line segment being replaced by a 'Z' shape, then each segment of that 'Z' being replaced by a smaller 'Z', ad infinitum.

sections.title: Crossing the Finite-Infinite Bridge
sections.content: Define the relationship between finite steps and the infinite limit. Explain that while any finite step is just a line, the *limit* of the sequence is a curve that is 2-dimensional. This bridges the gap between discrete topology and continuous mapping.
sections.example: A 'Pixel-to-Coordinate' mapping: Demonstrating how a coordinate (x, y) can be uniquely mapped to a single scalar value 't' along the space-filling path.

sections.title: Real-World Application: The Hilbert Curve
sections.content: Show why this matters. Space-filling curves like the Hilbert Curve are used to map 2D data into 1D memory while preserving spatial locality (clustering nearby points together).
sections.example: A high-tech image processing robot scanning a photo; it uses a Hilbert curve to scan pixels so that similar colors stay grouped in memory for efficient compression.

sections.title: Conclusion: Reconciling Intuition
sections.content: Summarize the core takeaway: Mathematics allows us to stretch 1D objects into 2D spaces. The 'infinite' isn't just a concept; it’s a design tool to solve optimization problems in finite systems.
sections.example: A final visual of a complex circuit board layout designed using space-filling curves to minimize signal travel time.

A 2D square has area, infinite points.
Can a 1D line visit every 2D point?

lecture_lines: Iterative fractals start with a simple generator.
We replace segments with a new shape repeatedly.
Each step fills more of the square.

storyboard.title: Conclusion: Reconciling Intuition

They solve complex optimization problems efficiently.
